**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-03**
**Member: Jordan Hayes | Member ID: W671447302**
**Reference number: POC-92D596C7F2-83353**
**Service denied: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030**
**Plan: MedStar Family Choice DC (Commercial/ACA)**

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the lower back decompression surgery (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision and to approve the procedure.

**About the policy and criteria behind this denial**

I want to be straightforward with you about one thing at the start of this letter. The denial notice dated 2026-08-03 says the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not identify that policy by name, and I have not been given the text of the criteria that were applied to my request. For that reason, I am not quoting any plan language anywhere in this letter. Nothing below is presented as a quotation from the plan's policy, and I am not stating any required time period, visit count, or other threshold as though it came from the plan, because no such requirement has been shown to me in writing.

Instead, I am setting out exactly what is in my medical records, so the plan can compare those records to whatever criteria it applied.

**Request for the criteria applied to my determination**

I am asking the plan, in writing, to provide me free of charge the specific rule, guideline, protocol, or criterion that was relied on to deny this request. I understand the plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to give me the specific rule or criterion relied on for the denial, and licensing does not remove that obligation. Please send me **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with the title of the medical policy referenced in the denial notice. Without that text, I cannot see which element of the plan's own standard my records were found not to meet, and I cannot fully respond to the decision.

**The reason given was incomplete documentation — here is the documentation**

The stated reason for the denial is that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the prior authorization packet contains the following, all of which is in my records:

- **Symptom duration.** 18 months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised conservative care.** Supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 8 weeks, from 2026-04-14 to 2026-06-09, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial.** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection.** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29, which gave 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging correlating to the proposed surgery.** MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-06-16 showing L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Physical examination.** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- **Functional impact.** I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain into my right calf.
- **Surgical safety factors.** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.
- **Requesting surgeon.** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

Taken together, these records document a specific structural finding on imaging, an examination finding at the matching level, a defined symptom duration, a completed and supervised course of physical therapy with dates and visit counts, a documented medication trial, and a documented injection with only brief partial relief. If any one of these items was missing from the file the plan reviewed, please tell me which item it was, and I will ask my surgeon's office to send it. If the items above were in the file, then I am asking the plan to explain which part of its criteria the record does not satisfy, with reference to the criteria text I have requested above.

**What I am asking for**

1. That the plan overturn the denial dated 2026-08-03 and approve CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Lindqvist.
2. That the plan send me, free of charge, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, and the title of the medical policy cited in the denial notice.
3. That if the denial is not overturned, the plan identify in writing the specific document or clinical element it found missing, and the specific criterion that element relates to, so that it can be supplied.

I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with relevant expertise in spine surgery, and I am happy to have my surgeon's office provide any additional records on request. Records may be requested from [surgeon's office name, address, phone, and fax].

**Timeliness and submission.** The denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-01-30**. I am submitting this appeal within that period. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is not the correct destination for member appeals, please redirect it and let me know, and I will also call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for taking the time to look at this again. This surgery is what my surgeon has documented that I need, and I would like the plan's decision to be based on the full record described above.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Hayes**
Member ID: W671447302
Reference number: POC-92D596C7F2-83353

[Signature]
[Date]

Enclosures: [list what you send — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-03; physical therapy discharge note; MRI report dated 2026-06-16; surgeon's office notes; medication and injection records]
